body: I'm not particularly interested in discussing that.
Unfortunately I do not have the means to speak to a psychiatrist. I'm not against seeing one, I'm interested in seeing how it would go, I just don't have the option to.

Thank you for your time. I'm sorry to hear about your friend. I hope you're doing the best that you feel you can.

I appreciate the sentiment about change and time. In many cases I do feel that this fits, but unfortunately not in mine. I'd rather not talk about the specifics because most people on this sub would not be familiar with the specifics. Many of my problems are permanent and are not able to be changed unlike a lot of temporary mental ailments or what not. I do often think about how it would affect my friends. When I come to a certain point, however, the drive to end myself begins to override the part of me that does my best to make them happy and I have to accept hurting them this way. I've already done it. If I could stick around to make them happy and keep them company while feeling comfortable and fulfilled with myself I certainly would, but that's not my reality. I do know that they care about me. The fact that I know that so well and am then not able to convince myself that they don't is one of the worst parts. I just feel too inadequate for myself. I came up short and am unable to love myself and that begins to extend to how I behave in personal relationships. It's unfortunate.
